title: Keep status service rows consistent with degraded health
prompt:
Fix the contradictory service indicators on /status. Evidence: src/app/status/page.tsx:37-43 stores the parsed health response, including a degraded response, while src/app/status/page.tsx:189-193 assigns operational to every service whenever the health object exists. The banner already checks health.status. A local execution of the actual component with status="degraded" rendered the Degraded banner alongside five operational service rows.

Change only src/app/status/page.tsx in production. Derive the service-row label from the existing aggregate health state: checking before completion, operational for ok, degraded for degraded, and down for the existing unreachable/error state. Give degraded rows an amber treatment. Preserve the polling interval and existing banner/history behavior; do not add individual service probes or imply that the aggregate endpoint measures each service independently.

Add tests/status-service-degradation.test.mjs using the existing TypeScript-transpile and mocked React-hook pattern. Render the real page for initial loading, ok, degraded, and fetch rejection; assert the visible service labels and their colors, including that a degraded response never produces operational rows. Run node --test tests/status-service-degradation.test.mjs tests/bazaar-health-query-errors.test.mjs. The latter existing tests passed during planning. This frontend defect is distinct from merged PR #24, which fixed the health endpoint. work on the assigned branch you are on. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, workflow, package.json, or auth changes.
